memory_update.text: PLPC should be tracked as an early-order signal for transmission buildout, with a possible 6-12 month lead versus downstream EPC and utility construction activity.
HPS.A is a cleaner physical-power bottleneck than HON for AI infrastructure screening because it sits in transformers and power-quality equipment rather than a diluted mega-cap conversion asset.
Need company filings and transcripts to quantify backlog, customer concentration, and lead-time signals for PLPC, HPS.A, ACA, VMI, and AZZ before promoting any of them to later Serenity layers.
Need to verify how much of HON's conversion asset is economically material, and whether LEU or BWXT better captures the investable nuclear bottleneck depending on policy and contract visibility.

summary: This chunk splits into two linked energy bottleneck lanes: (1) grid transmission / utility hardware, where PLPC, HUBB, ACA, VMI, and AZZ map as upstream-to-downstream beneficiaries of transmission, distribution, and structure buildout; and (2) nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks, where HON is a diluted conversion proxy, BWXT is the cleaner public reference for advanced fuel fabrication, and LEU is the thinner, more policy-dependent shadow play. HPS.A sits as a separate but adjacent physical-power bottleneck tied to transformers and power-quality equipment for data centers and electrification. The core research question is whether orders and backlog at smaller hardware suppliers lead or confirm broader grid and nuclear capex cycles.
